Hmm it I'm not sure what four Equal' is supposed to achieve, but I assume It's supposed to test, that the four given numbers are equal.

What haskell would try to do in your fourEqual' is, that it would try to test if threeEqual boolean and (q==n). If i understand your logic correctly, what you want is a function that checks if the first three parameters are equal and then check if the last one is equal to any of the first three. The way to do this would be 

fourEqual' m n p q = (m == n) && threeEqual n p q

What I think confused you can be shown in this example

twoEqual n = threeEqual n n

in this case not all parameters to threeEqual are given. It still works however because of a key property of haskell functions. There is no such thing as a function with multiple parameters in haskell everything is a function with one parameter, that can give you one of two things as a result:

  1. A function (which you can apply again to an other value) or
  2. A value
